data.narrative:
The Spaceport Company is a seed-stage space and aerospace venture that has raised $2M to date. The valuation universe includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning the sector, though the peer set lacks sufficient depth at identical or adjacent stages for direct median-based triangulation.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis, anchored to the $2M total raised as a proxy for seed-stage valuation, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression. This yields an implied valuation of $5M. The public comp universe in Space & Aerospace trades at a 25.3x median price-to-sales multiple across the five tickers, but this cannot be applied without disclosed revenue for the target. Peer-median anchoring was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum density thresholds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M–$6M, with a median point of $5M. Given reliance on a single method, key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x stage multiplier for this specific subsector and stage, the absence of revenue data to calibrate against public multiples, and limited private peer visibility at seed stage. A post-raise round or revenue guidance would materially sharpen this estimate.
